rot.plan.title: How this rotation works
rot.plan.intro: A rotation is the order in which crops alternate on the same field. This sequence repeats every {years} year(s). Month by month, the field goes through these stages:
rot.plan.grain: {from} → {to} · {crop}: sown at the start and harvested at the end ({days} days in the field).
rot.plan.second: {from} → {to} · {crop} as a second crop: sown right after the previous harvest, with no fallow, to get two crops in the same year ({days} days).
rot.plan.cover: {from} → {to} · {crop} as a cover crop: not harvested. It covers the soil in those months and is terminated at the end (herbicide or roller); its residue stays as mulch for the next crop ({days} days).
rot.plan.pasture: {from} → {to} · {crop} as pasture: it occupies the field all year and is cut or grazed.
rot.plan.fallow: {from} → {to} · Fallow ({days} days): the field has no crop. Weeds are controlled (herbicide or tillage), the soil stores water and the next sowing is prepared.
rot.plan.legume: {crop} is a legume: it fixes nitrogen from the air and leaves part in the soil for the next crop.
rot.plan.phLow: With the soil's pH {ph}, {crop} is below its range ({range}): lime before this stage.
rot.plan.phHigh: With the soil's pH {ph}, {crop} is above its range ({range}): alkaline soil for this crop.
rot.plan.restart: After the last stage, the sequence starts again with {crop}.
rot.plan.restartFallow: {from} → {to} · Fallow ({days} days), then the sequence starts again with {crop}.
rot.term.fallow.def: A period with no crop between a harvest and the next sowing. Weeds are controlled and the soil stores water.
rot.term.cover.def: A crop that is not harvested: it is sown to protect the soil from erosion, add organic matter and hold back weeds.
rot.term.second.def: A crop sown right after harvesting another in the same season, for example soybean after wheat.
rot.term.pasture.def: Perennial forage, such as alfalfa, that occupies the field for several years and is cut or grazed.
rot.term.legume.def: The soybean, vetch, pea and alfalfa family: their roots fix nitrogen from the air with bacteria.
rot.tech.waterOk: Water balance of the sequence: {mm} mm a year to spare (average rain minus what the crops use).
rot.tech.waterShort: Water balance of the sequence: {mm} mm a year short between average rain and what the crops use; soil reserves must cover the gap.
rot.tech.bare: Soil without a living crop: {days} days a year. With {infiltration} infiltration, erosion risk stays {erosion}.
rot.tech.residue: Residue: {t} t/ha a year of dry matter returned to the soil, sustaining organic matter.
rot.tech.families: {n} botanical families in the sequence; {breaks} breaks in the pest and disease cycle.
rot.tech.phOk: Soil pH {ph}: inside the range of every crop in the sequence that has a reference.
rot.tech.phOut: Soil pH {ph}: outside the range of {crops}.
recs.tech.balance: Cycle water balance: {rain} mm of average rain against {need} mm of crop demand, balance {balance} mm ({pct} % of demand covered by rain).
recs.tech.balanceYear: Annual water balance: {rain} mm of average rain against {need} mm of annual demand, balance {balance} mm ({pct} % covered by rain).
recs.tech.season.la_nina: Expected climate: La Niña (ONI {oni} °C, {period}). Here, October–March rain changed {effect} % in those years; {wet} mm of the cycle falls in October–March of the {season} season, so expected rain is {expected} mm and the balance {balance} mm.
recs.tech.season.el_nino: Expected climate: El Niño (ONI {oni} °C, {period}). Here, October–March rain changed {effect} % in those years; {wet} mm of the cycle falls in October–March of the {season} season, so expected rain is {expected} mm and the balance {balance} mm.
recs.tech.season.neutral: Expected climate: neutral phase (ONI {oni} °C, {period}), no El Niño or La Niña signal. Rain close to average is expected: {expected} mm, balance {balance} mm.
recs.tech.season.outside: Expected climate: the cycle does not fall in October–March of the {season} season, where the current ENSO phase acts; average rain is used for this crop.
recs.tech.frostOk: Frost: the whole cycle falls inside the zone's frost-free period.
recs.tech.frostRisk: Frost: part of the cycle falls in the frost period, with damage risk at emergence or flowering.
recs.tech.cover: Cover: the crop occupies the field {days} days; the rest of the year the soil is bare and more exposed to erosion.
recs.tech.different: Rotation: different botanical family from the previous crop, breaking the cycle of that family's pests and diseases.
recs.tech.same: Rotation: same botanical family as the previous crop, keeping its pests and diseases in the field.
recs.outlook.la_nina: Climate for the {season} season: La Niña per NOAA's ONI index ({oni} °C, {period}). Here, October–March rain was {nina} % from average in La Niña years and {nino} % in El Niño years (NASA POWER daily data since 2001). A historical tendency, not a forecast.
recs.outlook.el_nino: Climate for the {season} season: El Niño per NOAA's ONI index ({oni} °C, {period}). Here, October–March rain was {nino} % from average in El Niño years and {nina} % in La Niña years (NASA POWER daily data since 2001). A historical tendency, not a forecast.
recs.outlook.neutral: Climate for the {season} season: neutral phase per NOAA's ONI index ({oni} °C, {period}), so average rain is used. For reference, El Niño years here had {nino} % and La Niña years {nina} % October–March rain. A historical tendency, not a forecast.
recs.outlook.noHistory: Next season's climate: NOAA ONI index {oni} °C ({period}). There is not enough local rain history to measure its effect, so average rain is used.
recs.outlook.none: No El Niño/La Niña data available: balances use the zone's average rain.

rot.commonMeasures: Prevention measures common to these rotations
rot.soilUsed: The comparison uses rainfall, frost and parcel slope. It also considers how long the soil stays covered and estimated infiltration when evaluating soil protection.
rot.seq.help: How to read it: each row is a crop of the rotation and the bar is the 12 months of the year, January to December. Green marks the months that crop is in the field, from sowing to harvest or termination. Brown marks the months it is not; if no other crop fills them, the field is in fallow.

rot.fallow.title: Months without a crop: what to do with the land
rot.fallow.tip.weeds: Control weeds: walk the field every 2–3 weeks and spray before they set seed. Weeds use the water and nutrients the next crop needs.
rot.fallow.tip.residue: Leave the previous crop's residue on the surface and do not till (no-till): it shields the soil from sun, rain and wind and keeps moisture.
rot.fallow.tip.cover: This is a long autumn-winter period: sow a cover crop (rye or oats) so the soil is not left bare. Terminate it a few weeks before sowing {before}.
rot.fallow.tip.coverForMaize: This is a long autumn-winter period before maize: sow vetch as a cover crop. It protects the soil and, as a legume, leaves nitrogen for the maize. Terminate it a few weeks before sowing.
rot.fallow.tip.soilTest: Take soil samples (0–20 cm) to measure pH, phosphorus and nitrogen, and plan the fertilization of {before}.
rot.fallow.tip.lime: The soil pH ({ph}) is below what a crop of the rotation needs: this is the time to lime, since lime takes months to act.
rot.fallow.tip.sowPrep: A few weeks before sowing {before}: final weed control (chemical fallow), check the profile moisture and get seed and planter ready.

gloss.def.ndvi: Satellite greenness index: high values = more active vegetation, low = bare or dry soil.
gloss.def.et: Water the soil and plant return to the air; it signals crop water demand.
gloss.def.anomaly: Difference from what is normal for that time of year, measured against previous years.
gloss.def.waterBalance: Available rain minus what the crop needs in its cycle; negative = deficit.
gloss.def.gdd: Useful heat (above 10 °C) a crop accumulates to complete its cycle.
gloss.def.et0: Reference evapotranspiration (mm/day): what a well-watered lawn would evaporate; the base for estimating how much water a crop needs.
gloss.def.soilAnomaly: Difference between the soil moisture the satellite sees and what is normal for this time of year (%); negative = drier than usual.
gloss.def.frost: Day with a minimum temperature of 0 °C or less. On the calendar, the fraction of the month's days meeting that condition.
gloss.def.frostFree: Stretch of the year without likely frosts (days): between the last spring frost and the first autumn one.
gloss.def.satGround: A satellite pixel averages several km² and does not know your plot's exact elevation; that is why it can differ from a station inside the field.
gloss.def.bareSoil: Months with no living crop or cover (low NDVI); the soil is left exposed to erosion.
gloss.def.enso: ONI index of the Pacific phase: El Niño usually brings more rain to the Pampas; La Niña, less.
gloss.def.hydroGroup: Soil hydrologic group (A–D): how fast water infiltrates; A infiltrates a lot, D tends to pond.

demo.pampa.name: La Aurora ranch
demo.pampa.producer: Example producer: a family growing rainfed grain south-east of Chacabuco; worried about drought, El Niño and fire.
demo.producer: Example producer: a family running drip irrigation from a well, worried about frost, water and fire coming from the neighbouring brushland.
demo.disclaimer: Example producer and farm. The location and satellite data are real; the producer, names and economic figures are made up for the demo.
demo.saved: Saved result from {date}: the latest real reading available.
demo.tour.title: Tour of the example
demo.tour.parcels.title: The parcels and their crops
demo.tour.parcels.body: The field is split into three parcels, each with its own crop. Each colour is a crop.
demo.tour.badges.title: The fire and water badges
demo.tour.badges.body: Above each parcel the map shows its two main risks: fire probability and how dry the soil is.
demo.tour.alerts.title: Alerts come first
demo.tour.alerts.body: When something needs attention — a nearby hotspot or very dry soil — it sits on top of everything, with its emergency button.
demo.tour.priorities.title: Your priorities
demo.tour.priorities.body: In this tab you order the risks you care about most and enter your figures; the analysis rearranges itself.
demo.tour.more.title: More information
demo.tour.more.body: The detailed diagnosis, the hidden risks and the data sources are always one tap away, without crowding the view.
